description: Luckfox Aura (Rockchip RV1126B: quad Cortex-A53, 3 TOPS NPU), a board record: Atlas flashes it from maskrom (rockusb) with Rockchip's loader file and no vendor tool. Its USB id 2207:110b is a guess (pid_unconfirmed), and the record's chip check stops a flash on another chip. Written from Luckfox's wiki, Waveshare's product page, the board schematic and rkbin; untested on this board.

ram.this_record: UNCONFIRMED: the board in hand's LPDDR4X size

network.ethernet: Gigabit through the GMAC to an external PHY U25 (schematic; part UNCONFIRMED); a gigabit PoE header, not fitted
network.wifi_bt: Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5.4 on module U19 (schematic; part UNCONFIRMED)

ports: DC 5 V in on a USB-C DCIN connector (no Power Delivery); 5 V / 3 A
USB 3.0 OTG Type-C: the flashing port (the USB data port)
Four USB 2.0 host ports behind a CH334F hub (schematic U14)
MIPI CSI: two 4-lane connectors, CSI0 H3 and CSI1 H4 (22-pin)
MIPI DSI: connectors H2 and H7
hardware.fan: none; an unlabelled 3-pin SH1.0 header H6 in the schematic is UNCONFIRMED as a fan connector

camera.connectors: two 4-lane MIPI CSI connectors, 22-pin (CSI0 H3, CSI1 H4)

storage_target_evidence: wiki.luckfox.com Aura introduction and Waveshare's product page: eMMC optional (0, 8 or 64 GB) and a microSD slot as standard; no SPI-NAND or SPI-NOR is listed.
Atlas writes the image to the eMMC from byte 0, as for the other eMMC boards. Gaia has no Aura board config, so the image's layout is UNCONFIRMED (todo).
instructions: Power the Aura off. Short its two Maskrom pads (their position is UNCONFIRMED: see todo) with a wire or tweezers.
Connect the USB 3.0 Type-C flashing port to this computer with a data cable, then power the board on with the pads still shorted.

The board appears in maskrom as 2207:110b (RV1126B; the PID is a guess, so Atlas also checks the chip the board reports). Atlas runs the loader's DDR init and usbplug, writes the image to the eMMC, reads it back and restarts the board.
todo: 2207:110b is a guess (pid_unconfirmed): U-Boot's default for RV1126 is 0x110b (a search snippet, weak evidence). rkdeveloptool 304f073 has no 110x line, and the record is NOT 2207:110c (the RV1106's). Plug-in check: lsusb -d 2207: on the board in maskrom.

The loader: rkbin 3e288fe814e059dd06833495f845cab04ac20a5c (the short hash is the one the facts name), RKBOOT/RV1126BMINIALL.ini (NAME=RV110F): DDR rv1126b_ddr_1332MHz_v1.10, usbplug rv1126b_usbplug_v1.03, SPL rv1126b_spl_v1.06 (LOAD_ADDR 0x4fe00000), merged by boot_merger into rv1126b_loader_v1.10.106.bin. rkbin does not publish the merged file. Gaia needs: the merged loader (rv1126b_loader_v*.bin) and an Aura image (a whole eMMC disk, or the layout the SDK's RK_BOOT_MEDIUM uses: UNCONFIRMED).

UNCONFIRMED: the chip the loader reports. The loader header's chip field for RV110F is not checked here: it is reversed ASCII of either 'RV110F' ('110F') or '1126'. Atlas checks that number as a substring of platform.soc ('RV1126B' has '1126', not '110F'), so a '110F' board is refused before writing. Check the first trace on the board; if it reports 110F, set platform.soc to a name that contains it.
UNCONFIRMED: whether the board in hand has the eMMC fitted (lsblk), and the eMMC layout the image uses (the SDK's partition string is not confirmed).
UNCONFIRMED: where the two Maskrom pads are (the Getting Started page says only 'short the two pads'). Check the silkscreen or the schematic.
UNCONFIRMED: LED polarity and colours (LED1 on GPIO0_B3, LED2 on GPIO0_B4, each through 510 ohm). Check on the board by lighting each.
UNCONFIRMED: the Ethernet PHY part (U25) and the Wi-Fi/Bluetooth module part (U19).
UNCONFIRMED: the RAM size of the board in hand (1, 2 or 4 GB).
UNCONFIRMED: whether the unlabelled header H6 is a fan connector.
